Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level “Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy.” We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.
. Research strategies that rely predominantly on iterative trial-and-error experimentation are increasingly inadequate for navigating the scale and complexity of modern chemical and genomic spaces
. As a result, the pharmaceutical industry faces growing pressure to adopt new paradigms that move beyond incremental efficiency gains and instead provide mechanistic insight and predictive power capable of reducing late-stage failure. Driven by this practical demand, computational methods in drug discovery have continuously evolved, gradually transitioning from experience-driven auxiliary tools to a technological foundation capable of participating in core decision-making
To address this need, the methodological framework in drug discovery has undergone a continuous evolution from classical machine learning and deep learning to generative modeling. {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=What+mechanisms+allow+artificial+agents+to+evaluate+the+interestingness+or+scientific+priority+of+open-ended+problems+without+external+benchmarks%3F&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists\", \"abstract\": null, \"doi\": null, \"pmid\": \"PMC13658227\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13658227\", \"source\": \"PMC\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13658227/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13658227/pdf/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"From the logic of coordination to goal-directed reasoning: the agentic turn in artificial intelligence.\", \"abstract\": \"The rise of agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) marks a transition from systems that optimize externally specified objectives to systems capable of representing, evaluating, and revising their own goals. Whereas earlier AI architectures executed fixed task specifications, agentic systems maintain recursive loops of perception, evaluation, goal-updating, and action, allowing them to sustain and adapt purposive activity across temporal and organizational scales. This paper argues that Agentic AI is not an incremental extension of large language models (LLMs) or autonomous agents in the sense we know it from classical AI and multi-agent systems, but a reconstitution of agency itself within computational substrates. Building on the logic of coordination, delegation, and self-regulation developed in early agent-based process management systems, we propose a general theory of synthetic purposiveness, where agency emerges as a distributed and self-maintaining property of artificial systems operating in open-ended environments. We develop the concept of synthetic teleology-the engineered capacity of artificial systems to generate and regulate goals through ongoing self-evaluation-and we formalize its dynamics through a recursive goal-maintenance equation. We further outline design patterns, computational semantics, and measurable indicators of purposiveness (e.g., teleological coherence, adaptive recovery, and reflective efficiency), providing a foundation for the systematic design and empirical investigation of agentic behaviour. By reclaiming agency as a first-class construct in artificial intelligence, we argue for a paradigm shift from algorithmic optimization toward goal-directed reasoning and purposive orchestration-one with far-reaching epistemic, societal, and institutional consequences.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/frai.2025.1728738\", \"pmid\": \"41602311\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC12833085\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2025.1728738\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC12833085\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC12833085?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"A Review of Multi-Agent AI Systems for Biological and Clinical Data Analysis.\", \"abstract\": \"This review evaluates the emerging paradigm of multi-agent systems (MASs) for biomedical and clinical data analysis, focusing on their ability to overcome the reasoning and reliability limitations of standalone large language models (LLMs). We synthesize findings from recent architectural frameworks, specifically LangGraph, CrewAI, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), to examine how specialized agent teams divide labor, utilize precision tools, and cross-verify outputs. We find that MAS architectures yield significant performance gains in various domains: recent implementations improved oncology decision-making accuracy from 30.3% to 87.2% and reached a peak of 93.2% accuracy on USMLE-style benchmarks through simulated clinical evolution. In clinical trial matching, multi-agent frameworks achieved 87.3% accuracy and enhanced clinician screening efficiency by 42.6% (p < 0.001). However, we also highlight critical operational challenges, including an unreliability tax of 15-50× higher token consumption compared to standalone models and the risk of cascading errors where initial hallucinations are amplified across the agent collective. We conclude that while MAS enables a shift toward collaborative intelligence in biomedicine, its clinical and research adoption requires the development of deterministic orchestration and rigorous cost-utility frameworks to ensure safety and expert-centered oversight.\", \"doi\": \"10.3390/mps9020033\", \"pmid\": \"41874150\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13010680\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3390/mps9020033\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13010680\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13010680?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Beyond computational equivalence: the behavioral inference principle for machine consciousness.\", \"abstract\": \"Large Language Models (LLMs) have rapidly become a central topic in AI and cognitive science, due to their unprecedented performance in a vast array of tasks. Indeed, some even see \\\"sparks of artificial general intelligence\\\" in their apparently boundless faculty for conversation and reasoning. Their sophisticated emergent faculties, which were not initially anticipated by their designers, have ignited an urgent debate about whether and under which circumstances we should attribute consciousness to artificial entities in general and LLMs in particular. The current consensus, rooted in computational functionalism, proposes that consciousness should be ascribed based on a principle of computational equivalence. The objective of this opinion piece is to criticize this current approach and argue in favor of an alternative \\\"behavioral inference principle\\\", whereby consciousness is attributed if it is useful to explain (and predict) a given set of behavioral observations. We believe that a behavioral inference principle will provide an epistemologically valid and operationalizable criterion to assess machine consciousness.\", \"doi\": \"10.1093/nc/niag002\", \"pmid\": \"41704937\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC12907924\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/nc/niag002\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC12907924\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC12907924?pdf=render\"}]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "6f14401d55fad392d3e626cf2d768cfd3d4c5479f19bea1e8e7db515a60fa12c", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.3389/frai.2025.1728738", "doi:10.3390/mps9020033", "doi:10.1093/nc/niag002", "pmc:PMC13658227", "pmc:PMC12833085", "pmc:PMC13010680", "pmc:PMC12907924"], "source_candidates": ["https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13658227/?tool=EBI", "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13658227/pdf/?tool=EBI", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227?pdf=render", "https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2025.1728738", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC12833085", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC12833085?pdf=render", "https://doi.org/10.3390/mps9020033"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}

review.would_change_mind: Evidence that fixed-interval updates consistently outperform discrepancy-driven evaluation in long-term open-ended tasks.

claims.statement: Discrepancy-driven evaluation allows autonomous systems to maintain operational relevance by detecting outdated knowledge and adapting cognitive strategies in changing environments.

support.explanation: Provides a mechanism for autonomous agents to evaluate the ongoing utility of their knowledge, which is essential for problem formulation in open-ended contexts.
support.passage: The framework also incorporates discrepancy-driven evaluation to detect when previously valid knowledge or capabilities have become outdated.

review.alternative: Single-agent curiosity-driven discovery without explicit multi-agent coordination.
review.would_change_mind: Benchmarks showing single-agent models achieving equivalent or superior discovery rates in complex, multi-variable environments.

claims.statement: Autonomous multi-agent evolution frameworks enable effective open-ended discovery by allowing agents to collaborate and share memory, outperforming fixed heuristic baselines.

support.explanation: Highlights the effectiveness of agent autonomy over rigid rule-based systems in open-ended search.
support.passage: CORAL replaces rigid control with long-running agents that explore, reflect, and collaborate through shared persistent memory, asynchronous multi-agent execution, and heartbeat-based interventions.
